message.content: {"summary":"Your report presents a well-structured GBR-monitoring mission with genuine STK evidence covering launch, SSO orbit, ground station and EOL. However, a critical inclination error (87.79° vs your own plot's ~97.9°), an incorrect Kourou latitude, a misread access statistic, and citation/labelling weaknesses held the design and presentation criteria at Adequate. Fixing these factual and presentation issues is your clearest path to Accomplished.","next_steps":["Correct the inclination: verify the sun-synchronous value at 600 km (~97.8°, retrograde) against your own STK plot, and re-check any downstream calculations that used 87.79°.","Fix the Kourou latitude (~5.2°N, not 45.05°N) and re-examine your launch-window reasoning, which depends on it; also restate the mean access duration (580.8 s ≈ 9.7 min) accurately.","Name your operator entity and customer groups explicitly in the Introduction, and state whether STK scenario files are attached in an appendix.","Replace Wikipedia with primary/technical sources, give full reference details (titles, access dates), and number all figures and tables consistently with in-text citations.","Tighten the EOL section: remove the graveyard-orbit discussion (inapplicable in LEO) and resolve the contradictory thruster/passive-disposal sentences."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your mission rationale (Great Barrier Reef monitoring) and single-spacecraft justification are well argued and referenced. To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify the operator (which organisation runs the spacecraft?) and the customer groups (e.g. reef researchers, agencies), rather than leaving users implied by 'accessed from Australian ground facilities'.","C2":"All major requirements are addressed with STK screenshots and an access report, which is good practice. However, the stated 87.79° inclination contradicts your own plot (~97.9°) and your 'retrograde SSO' description; Kourou's latitude is ~5.2°N, not 45.05°N, affecting your launch-window logic; and 580.8 s is ~10 min, not 'almost twenty minutes'. Also mention your STK scenario files. Resolving these errors and inconsistencies is what the Accomplished level requires.","C3":"Your conclusions summarise each segment and sensibly flag the Vega E availability risk with a fallback. To reach Accomplished, add quantitative synthesis — e.g. revisit coverage vs reef-monitoring needs, data volumes vs contact time — rather than restating body content generically.","C4":"Your structure is logical with a clear executive summary, but figures lack numbers, tables are unlabelled, references are bare URLs without titles or dates, and Wikipedia is disallowed. Grammar slips ('a Earth observation satellite', 'which is also desirable') also appear. Consistent figure/table numbering and proper referencing are required for the Accomplished level."}}
